ui.chat.status.credential_refused.role: title of the chat status strip when the running server refused this app's credential
ui.chat.status.credential_refused.tone: statement of fact plus its consequence, sentence case, trailing period
ui.chat.status.credential_refused.note: The strip's own sentence for this root cause. It tells the reader why their credential was refused, while the control beside it says Retry: the renderer has no sign-in path, so 'Sign in' would name an act the app cannot perform.

ui.chat.status.degraded.role: title of the chat status strip when the connection is up but the server is answering slowly
ui.chat.status.degraded.tone: statement plus what happens to the reader's messages, sentence case, trailing period
ui.chat.status.degraded.note: Drawn only when the server is reachable: a dead process must not be described as slow. Nothing has failed here - it is a fact about latency.

ui.chat.status.internet_offline.role: title of the chat status strip when this machine has no network at all
ui.chat.status.internet_offline.tone: statement plus what happens to a send, sentence case, trailing period
ui.chat.status.internet_offline.note: The subject is THIS machine, not the server: on a machine with no network, blaming the server would send the reader to the wrong remedy.

ui.chat.status.unreachable.role: title of the chat status strip when nothing is answering
ui.chat.status.unreachable.tone: statement plus what happens to a send, sentence case, trailing period
ui.chat.status.unreachable.note: Covers both 'no server is there' and 'a daemon is there that this app did not attach to': the reader's position is the same, and main's own detail line says which path was taken.
